label: original-phase input of v/e/u/x/h/i/d/m/j/3 after an earlier q/l/a/p/g/y/2
predicate: (phase==0) & (t>=2) & isin(in_tok,[tok(c) for c in "veuxhidmj3"]) & seen([tok(c) for c in "qlapgy2"])
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, at t>=2. It is essentially silent on the delimiter and the copy phase (13 of 64.7k dev activations). It needs two things: the current input is one of a group of tokens (v strongest at 4.7x lift, then e, u, x, h, i, d, m, j, and weakly 3), and the earlier prefix holds a token from a second group (q, l, a, p, g, y, 2). Starting with q/l/a/y/2 gives the strongest activations. The rate rises with position, peaks around orig_idx 5-6 and is higher near the end of the input (to_go 0-1). It is mostly on the first occurrence of the input token (90% of mass). Top activations (about 0.23) are v/e right after a prefix like y q p a k or q a z p z z. It does NOT fire at t=0-1, on o/t or most other letters, or when the prefix lacks the q/l/a/p/g/y/2 group. Precision is limited (~0.53): the same token and context often stay below threshold, so magnitude seems to depend on how much of the prefix is in the trigger group (an inference I did not check directly). Requiring two or more such tokens raises precision to 0.71 but halves recall.
